items.title: Imagine the SOC Without a Queue: From Alert Backlog to AI Hypothesis Engine
items.description: The SOC we've always known was built around a model that guarantees most of the alert queue will never receive analyst review. There's never time. In a traditional SOC, the typical progression follows a well-known pattern: an alert arrives; a detection engine assigns a severity score. items.description: Attackers are now exploiting a critical-severity vulnerability in the Gitea self-hosted Git service, according to the U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA). [...]

items.title: The MFA Identity Trap: When Authentication Creates a False Sense of Security
items.description: Organizations must distinguish identity verification, authentication and threat detection, or risk successfully authenticating the attackers they are trying to stop. The post The MFA Identity Trap: When Authentication Creates a False Sense of Security appeared first on SecurityWeek.

items.title: Chrome 152 Patches Over 300 Vulnerabilities
items.description: Most of the flaws were discovered by Google using AI, but researchers are still discovering high-value Chrome vulnerabilities. The post Chrome 152 Patches Over 300 Vulnerabilities appeared first on SecurityWeek.

items.title: Finding Nemo(Claw): Networking Issue Allows for LLM Poisoning in OpenClaw
items.description: Attackers can exploit a security bug in Nvidia's tool to gain unauthenticated access to the local model server through the Ollama API, paving the way for persistent AI agent corruption.
